brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.requirement: Two-storey storage tower for a workbench
requirements.evidence: Two storeys: level 0 has full hex bases at (0,0), (1,0) with notch drawer frames at (0,1) and (1,-1); level 1 has a full base at (0,0,1) holding a full-depth bin. Open faces capped and joints locked; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
Two notch drawer frames (notch:0#0,1#notch1 fm hand and notch:0#1,-1#notch4 mf hand) on the lower storey, each filling the empty position between two touching bases.
The tower is a compact 1-column footprint of about 2 cells by 2 levels; I did not verify its mounting or height against a specific bench, and the configurator does not check bench attachment or load.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex tower: bases at (0,0) and (1,0) on the lower level with two notch drawer frames beside them, and a second storey at (0,0,1) with a full-depth bin. Open faces are capped and joints locked; the configurator reports no issues and clear meshes. Materials, load capacity and bench fixing are not checked by the configurator.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
